text:
Michael Carcone is a fourth-line energy forward for Utah who keeps shooting and keeps missing. He has 1 goal on 29 shots in 14 games, a 3.4% shooting percentage against a range of about 9.5% to 14% for him, and 2.45 expected goals on his own shots.

It's a small sample, but the pattern matters because the rest of his game is solid. Utah controls 55% of the shot attempts and 56% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on, though that is about what the team does without him. He has 37 hits in 12.4 minutes a night, and his top speed is in the 88th percentile in NHL Edge tracking.

Last season Evolving-Hockey had his team creating more with him on the ice than with almost any other forward (95th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking showed a player who carries the puck in on 54% of his entries and makes 18% of his setups from behind the net, more than double the typical forward. The tools for more than 3 points are there. Utah has also scored 3.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on. Watch for the bounces to even out.
headline: Shooting, not scoring
